topics.title: A Framework for System Design Interviews
topics.description: A structured approach to solving open-ended system design interview questions effectively.

subtopics.title: Why We Need a Framework
subtopics.theory:
1️⃣ Why We Need a Framework

✅ Interview Definition

A system design framework is a structured approach used to solve open-ended design problems in a clear, scalable, and interview-friendly way.

🔎 Why Important

System design questions:

Have no single correct answer

Are vague intentionally

Test thinking, not memorization

Without a framework:

You jump randomly into components

You miss requirements

You over-engineer early

🎯 What Interviewer Evaluates

Structured thinking

Trade-off reasoning

Scalability awareness

Communication clarity

subtopics.title: The 4-Step System Design Framework
subtopics.theory:
2️⃣ The 4-Step System Design Framework (Core of Chapter)

This is the heart of Chapter 3.

subtopics.title: Step 1: Clarify Requirements
subtopics.theory:
🟢 STEP 1: Clarify Requirements

✅ Interview Definition

Clarifying requirements means identifying what the system must do (functional) and how well it must perform (non-functional).

📌 Functional Requirements

Definition

Features the system must support.

Examples:

Upload photo

Send message

Search video

📌 Non-Functional Requirements

Definition

Quality attributes that define system performance.

Examples:

Scalability

Availability

Latency

Consistency

Durability

📖 New Terms

Scalability

Ability to handle increasing traffic without performance degradation.

Availability

Percentage of time system remains operational.

Latency

Time taken to respond to a request.

Consistency

All users see same data at the same time.

Durability

Data is not lost after it is written.

🎯 Important Points

Always ask about:

Expected users

Read vs Write ratio

Data size

Real-time requirement

Never assume silently

State assumptions clearly

⚠️ Mistake

Starting design without clarifying scope.

subtopics.title: Step 2: Back-of-the-Envelope Estimation
subtopics.theory:
🟢 STEP 2: Back-of-the-Envelope Estimation

(Uses Chapter 2 concepts)

✅ Interview Definition

Back-of-the-envelope estimation is rough mathematical calculation to estimate scale and feasibility of a system.

📌 What to Estimate

DAU (Daily Active Users)

QPS (Queries Per Second)

Storage

Bandwidth

📖 New Terms

DAU

Number of users active per day.

QPS

Number of requests per second.

Bandwidth

Amount of data transferred per second.

🎯 Why Important

Helps choose DB type

Helps decide caching

Helps detect bottlenecks

Shows interviewer you think at scale

⚠️ Disadvantage

Numbers are approximate

Not exact science

👉 But interviewers care about reasoning, not perfect numbers.

subtopics.title: Step 3: High-Level Design
subtopics.theory:
🟢 STEP 3: High-Level Design

✅ Interview Definition

High-level design is a block-level architectural view of major system components and how they interact.

📌 Components Usually Included

Client (Web / Mobile)

Load Balancer

Web Servers

Database

Cache

CDN

Message Queue

📖 New Terms

Component

Independent functional block in system.

Architecture

Overall structure of system.

API

Interface through which services communicate.

🎯 Important Rules

Do NOT start with schema

Do NOT go too deep early

Draw big boxes first

Explain request flow

✅ Advantages

Shows structured thinking

Easy to modify

Gives big picture

❌ Disadvantages

Doesn’t show deep expertise yet

May hide bottlenecks

subtopics.title: Step 4: Deep Dive
subtopics.theory:
🟢 STEP 4: Deep Dive

✅ Interview Definition

Deep dive means analyzing one or two critical components in detail.

📌 What to Deep Dive

Database schema

Caching strategy

Sharding logic

Replication model

Consistency model

Rate limiting

Message queue processing

📖 New Terms

Bottleneck

Component limiting system performance.

Replication

Copying data across servers.

Sharding

Splitting data across multiple DBs.

🎯 Important Strategy

Pick component with highest risk

Justify your choice

Discuss trade-offs

subtopics.title: Trade-Off Analysis
subtopics.theory:
3️⃣ Trade-Off Analysis (Very Important)

✅ Interview Definition

Trade-off analysis is evaluating advantages and disadvantages between different architectural choices.

📌 Common Trade-Offs

SQL vs NoSQL

SQL:

Strong consistency

ACID guarantees

Harder to scale writes

NoSQL:

Easy horizontal scaling

Flexible schema

Weaker consistency sometimes

Strong vs Eventual Consistency

Strong:

Always up-to-date data

Higher latency

Eventual:

Better availability

Faster

Temporary stale data

Cache vs Direct DB

Cache:

Fast

Reduces DB load

Stale data risk

Direct DB:

Fresh data

Slower

🎯 Interview Tip

There is no perfect choice.
Always say:

"Given X requirement, I prefer Y because..."

subtopics.title: Handling Bottlenecks
subtopics.theory:
4️⃣ Handling Bottlenecks

✅ Definition

A bottleneck is the slowest or most overloaded component that limits overall system performance.

Common Bottlenecks

Database

Network

Single machine CPU

Disk I/O

Solutions

Caching

Replication

Sharding

Load balancing

Asynchronous processing

subtopics.title: Communication Strategy
subtopics.theory:
5️⃣ Communication Strategy

✅ Interview Definition

System design communication is the ability to explain reasoning clearly while designing.

Important Points

Think aloud

Draw simple diagrams

State assumptions

Adapt when interviewer challenges

Red Flags

Silent designing

Defensive behavior

Random component naming

Overengineering early

subtopics.title: Time Management Strategy
subtopics.theory:
6️⃣ Time Management Strategy (Interview Hack)

Typical 45–60 min interview:

5–10 min → Clarify requirements

5–10 min → Estimation

15–20 min → High-level design

10–15 min → Deep dive

5 min → Scale discussion

subtopics.title: Common Mistakes in Interviews
subtopics.theory:
7️⃣ Common Mistakes in Interviews

❌ Skipping requirements
❌ Skipping estimation
❌ Designing everything in detail
❌ Ignoring failure cases
❌ Not discussing trade-offs

subtopics.title: What Interviewers Actually Evaluate
subtopics.theory:
8️⃣ What Interviewers Actually Evaluate

They check:

Can you handle ambiguity?

Do you think in scale?

Do you know distributed systems basics?

Can you reason trade-offs?

Can you communicate clearly?

They DO NOT check:

Perfect numbers

Fancy buzzwords

Memorized architecture diagrams

📌 Ultra-Clear Revision Sheet

Clarify requirements first

Estimate scale second

High-level architecture third

Deep dive critical parts

Always explain trade-offs
